# Guard & Security Requirements Checklist: Standardised Claude Code Cloud Environment

**Purpose**: A reviewer gate on whether the branch guard's requirements are complete, clear, consistent and
measurable enough to build from. It covers the rules, the exceptions, self-protection and fail-closed
behaviour (FR-005 to FR-014, FR-012a, FR-013a, and the related session-start rules).
**Created**: 2026-09-24
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) · [plan.md](../plan.md) · [contracts/hooks.md](../contracts/hooks.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

**Depth**: Standard · **Audience**: A reviewer, before the US1 implementation in lightspeedwp/.github#3524 starts

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Does FR-013a list every file that can switch the guard off? It now names `.claude/hooks/**`, `.claude/settings.json`, `.claude/settings.local.json` and `~/.claude/settings.json` (T001, research R12); confirm no other settings source can disable hooks. [Completeness, Spec §FR-013a]
- [x] CHK002 Does the spec define every write path the guard must police? The spec names git and "the GitHub integration" but doesn't say whether `gh api`, `gh pr create` or pushes to remotes other than `origin` are in scope. [Coverage, Gap, Spec §FR-006, §FR-008]
- [x] CHK003 Are requirements defined for who may turn off the enforcement switch, and where it can be set: the shared environment, a personal environment, or a developer's local shell? [Gap, Spec §FR-013, §FR-014]
- [x] CHK004 Are default values specified for when the switch and base-branch settings are missing, for example in a local session with no LightSpeed variables? [Gap, Spec §FR-013, §FR-014]
- [x] CHK005 Is the set of "protected" branches complete? The spec lists `main` and the configured base branch. Are `release/*` branches intentionally left out? [Completeness, Spec §FR-005]
- [x] CHK006 Is there an acceptance scenario for guard faults (FR-012a), as there is for self-protection (scenario 11)? [Gap, Spec §FR-012a, User Story 1]
- [x] CHK007 Does the spec say what the person using the session sees when the guard refuses something, as distinct from what the agent receives? [Gap, Spec §FR-011]

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK008 Is "branch operations" in FR-012a defined precisely enough to know which commands are refused during a guard fault? For example, is switching to an existing branch refused, or only creating one? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-012a]
- [x] CHK009 Is it clear which validator is "the same validation rules the repository's CI uses"? The repo has two, `lib/validate-branch-name.js` and `scripts/validation/validate-branch-name.cjs`, and the library's own comments call the `.cjs` file canonical. [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-010]
- [x] CHK010 Is "head of an open PR" defined for PRs from forks, or PRs opened against another repository, under the legacy PR exception? [Clarity, Spec §FR-006]
- [x] CHK011 Is "open-PR status can't be verified" defined in measurable terms, such as a timeout or specific failure conditions? The spec gives none; the plan uses 5 seconds per check. [Clarity, Measurability, Spec §FR-006]
- [x] CHK012 Are the documentation-exception paths defined so they can't be escaped? For example, does the spec cover path normalisation (`docs/../package.json`), symlinks, and case differences? [Clarity, Gap, Spec §FR-005]
- [x] CHK013 Is "suggest a corrected name where the validator can" specific enough to test? Should the suggestion itself be a valid name? [Measurability, Spec §FR-011]
- [x] CHK014 Is "a LightSpeed repository" in FR-009 defined, for example by GitHub owner? And is it clear that the `main` base rule applies only to `.github`? [Clarity, Spec §FR-009]
- [x] CHK015 Are the requirement IDs FR-012a and FR-013a ordered and cross-referenced so readers can find them? In the spec, FR-012a appears after FR-013. [Clarity, Traceability, Spec §Enforcement]

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK016 Is the documentation exception on `main` consistent with `CLAUDE.md` and the branching strategy, which say `main` holds production releases only? [Conflict, Spec §FR-005, Clarification Q1]
- [x] CHK017 Do FR-005 (commit), FR-006 (push) and FR-008 (GitHub writes) apply the legacy PR exception and the documentation exception in the same way, with the same verification rules? [Consistency, Spec §FR-005, §FR-006, §FR-008]
- [x] CHK018 Is the "session placeholder" defined the same way everywhere, including the naming pattern, so the guard and the session-start rules agree on what counts as a placeholder? [Consistency, Spec §FR-001, §FR-005, Key Entities]
- [x] CHK019 Is FR-012 (quoted text is ignored) consistent with FR-013a's shell parsing for guard-file edits? For example, is `echo "x" > .claude/settings.json` treated the same way in both places? [Consistency, Spec §FR-012, §FR-013a]
- [x] CHK020 Do the edge cases for protected branches agree with FR-005 and FR-006 on the documentation exception and bot-owned branches? [Consistency, Spec §Edge Cases, §FR-005]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [x] CHK021 Can each refusal rule (FR-005 to FR-009, FR-013a) be checked against a specific acceptance scenario with a defined input and expected outcome? [Measurability, Spec §User Story 1]
- [x] CHK022 Is a performance target for the guard written into the spec, as opposed to only the plan (150 ms per call, and up to 10 s for the legacy PR check)? [Gap, Non-Functional]
- [x] CHK023 Do the success criteria cover how often the guard refuses correct actions by mistake, not just whether branches end up compliant? [Gap, Spec §SC-001, §SC-007]

## Scenario & Edge Case Coverage

- [x] CHK024 Are requirements defined for unusual git states, such as detached HEAD, a rebase or merge in progress, worktrees, or pushing with a refspec to a different target branch? [Coverage, Edge Case, Gap]
- [x] CHK025 Are force-pushes to the agent's own compliant branch intentionally allowed, and is that written down? [Coverage, Gap, Spec §FR-006]
- [x] CHK026 Are the limits of shell parsing written down, so it's clear which constructions may slip past the guard (`eval`, aliases, `cd other && git …`)? And is CI named as the final gate? [Coverage, Assumption, Spec §Edge Cases, Assumptions]
- [x] CHK027 Do the guarantees for the automatic hard reset of fresh sessions (FR-002) rule out ever discarding untracked files or unpushed commits? [Coverage, Data Loss Risk, Spec §FR-002, §Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK028 Is the behaviour defined for when the guard itself can't run at all, for example if Node is missing so the hook never starts? And is that failing open recorded as a known limitation? [Gap, Exception Flow, Spec §FR-012a]

## Security Assumptions & Dependencies

- [x] CHK029 Is the threat model stated: is the guard meant to stop accidental non-compliance, or an agent actively trying to get around it? The self-protection and fault requirements (FR-012a, FR-013a) suggest the second. [Assumption, Gap]
- [x] CHK030 Is the dependency on GitHub branch protection's "require review from Code Owners" setting written down? Without it, the CODEOWNERS entry in FR-013a doesn't enforce an Owner's review. [Dependency, Gap, Spec §FR-013a]
- [x] CHK031 Is it recorded that the switch leaves no record when it's turned off, and that this was a deliberate choice given the no-telemetry decision (Q5)? [Assumption, Consistency, Spec §FR-013, Clarification Q5]
- [x] CHK032 Is the platform's push protection (only the current branch can be pushed) recorded as an assumption the requirements depend on, along with what happens if the platform changes it? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- CHK001 matches tasks.md T001. Resolving it closes both.
- Items that find real gaps (CHK001, CHK003, CHK009, CHK016, CHK029, CHK030) are best settled with `/speckit-clarify` before T020–T023 are built.

  items were already satisfied. The other 24 were settled by spec changes, recorded under "Session 2026-09-24
